answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may submit work, with rewards and reputation tied to that same on-chain account. A dawn of new accounts does not create free influence: each one needs its own deposit, and suspected fraud can forfeit it. Raising a bridge of disposable identities therefore ties up real capital, while splitting stake across accounts does not multiply voting weight. The copper in the attacker’s budget is exposed to loss for every identity they create.
